ops.oldText: Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement without such consent, except in the case where such transaction involves a direct competitor of the other party where consent of the other party will be required.
ops.newText: Notwithstanding the foregoing, (a) Corio shall have the right to assign this Agreement, without the consent of Commerce One, to any of its affiliates or in connection with the merger or acquisition of Corio or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement, and (b) Commerce One shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of Commerce One or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement without such consent, except in the case where such transaction involves a direct competitor of Corio, where the consent of Corio will be required. Any consent required under this Section 14.1 shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.

input.comment: [Playbook] We have added an affiliate/successor carve-out so that our internal reorganizations and M&A transactions do not require Commerce One's consent, and confined the direct-competitor consent exception to Commerce One's own assignments; a competitor veto over our change of control is off-market for us. We have also made any remaining consent subject to a reasonableness standard. As a fallback we can accept a mutual right to assign to affiliates and successors with prior written notice.
input.summary: Add affiliate/successor assignment right for Corio without consent, limit competitor-consent exception to Commerce One assignments, and add a reasonableness standard for consent.
